overview: White offers the e-pawn with 3.f3, in the manner of a Blackmar-Diemer. After 3...exf3 4.Nxf3 or 4.Qxf3 White has a lead in development and an open f-file for a kingside attack. Black can keep the pawn and usually consolidates with ...e6 and ...Nf6, so White scores on activity and surprise rather than a proven edge.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on f3 and develop quickly with Bc4, d4 and Bf4
Aim at f7 and the kingside with the f-file and the queen on f3

black_ideas.idea: Take on f3 and return the pawn only if it brings a safe, developed position
Play ...Nf6, ...e6, ...Be7 and castle, then trade pieces

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 against Black ...e6 or ...c6
Black a pawn up while White pieces are active

character.notes: Open position with White pieces developed fast and tactics against f7, but Black has a simple consolidating plan.

gambit.notes: 3...exf3 wins the e-pawn and White has no forced way to regain it.

soundness.notes: The pawn is not regained by force, so strong players consider White short of compensation, as in the Pseudo-Diemer.

structure.notes: Pawns come off in the centre and the f-file opens, so play is about open lines.

approach.notes: A rare sideline of an already rare 1.Nc3; strong players hardly choose it.

level.notes: Short gambit lines need some move-order knowledge, but it is unsound.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pseudo-Diemer Gambit, Dunst
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. Nc3 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. f3 exf3 4. Qxf3
sublines_that_differ.how: White recaptures with the queen rather than a knight, aiming for Bb5 and quick pressure on b7.

character.reason: Open lines, a pawn down for development and a Black king that must be careful make this concrete and risky.

gambit.reason: White gives the e-pawn and Black can keep it after ...exf3.

soundness.reason: The pawn is not regained and engines prefer Black, so it works mostly as a surprise.

structure.reason: The e-pawn trade and the f-file opening leave an open centre.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 1.Nc3, and this gambit even less.

level.reason: The lines are short but a dubious gambit is never a beginner choice.

plans.reason: White plays for fast development and pressure on f7 through the open f-file.
